completion_data.completion_summary: Rewrote check_duplicate_title() in literature-ingest-online.sh to use a single hard-timed (10s), fail-open .zotero-title-sim.py --batch invocation instead of one python3 subprocess per index.json title, added the --batch mode itself, wrote an 11-assertion regression suite (test-title-sim-dedup.sh, registered in manifest.json), and documented the contract. Measured full-index dedup check time on the real 11,793-entry index dropped from an observed 9-10 minutes (or 540s timeout) to ~0.7 seconds, with the WARNING text and 0.85 threshold preserved byte-for-byte and the 2-argv contract used by zotero-resolve-pdf.sh unchanged.

memory_candidates.content: When collapsing an O(n) per-item subprocess loop (e.g. one python3 invocation per candidate against a large index) into a single batch invocation, feed the candidate list via stdin rather than argv to avoid ARG_MAX limits, and wrap the batch call in a hard `timeout` with fail-open semantics (any non-zero exit/timeout/empty/unparseable output treated as 'no result found', function still returns success) so the optimization can never turn a recommendation-only check into a blocking one. Guard the assignment against `set -euo pipefail` aborting on the fail-open branch with `result="$(...)" || true` as a standalone assignment (not `local x=$(...)`, which masks the command substitution's exit status).

A deliberate-break regression check (revert a threshold/constant and confirm the test suite fails) is only meaningful if the near-duplicate/near-match test fixture actually exercises the comparison being guarded. A fixture that hits an earlier short-circuit path (e.g. an exact-normalized-equality match that always scores 1.0) will pass regardless of a threshold regression, silently defeating the deliberate-break check. Pick a fixture whose score falls strictly between the threshold and any short-circuit value.
